beats.lead: You would guess it came from a screen
beats.text: The word 'pixel' was first published for a space probe, not a display.
beats.note: Frederic Billingsley used it in two 1965 papers describing digitised images sent back from the Moon and Mars.

beats.name: Frederic Billingsley
beats.role: An engineer at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. His papers on processing planetary probe images may be the first place 'pixel' ever appeared in print.

beats.lead: He did not coin it himself
beats.text: He picked it up from someone else at a different company.
beats.note: Keith McFarland, at Link Division in Palo Alto, told him it was already 'in use' around 1963. McFarland did not know where it came from either.

beats.text: The word for the smallest piece of a picture arrived with no clean origin at all.

beats.line: Every screen you own is made of a word nobody can fully trace.
